articles.title: VRT MAX support lands in Music Assistant
articles.dek: A first contribution adds Flemish public radio, podcasts, favourites and listening progress to the server.
body: Bram Goolaerts’ newly merged provider connects Music Assistant with VRT MAX, the streaming service of the Flemish public broadcaster. It covers live stations including Radio 1, Radio 2, Studio Brussel, MNM and Klara, alongside listen-back programmes, podcasts and search. Live radio does not require an account.

Signing in enables on-demand playback, Mijn lijst library syncing and resume positions that carry across devices. Separate provider instances let people in one household keep their own accounts, while listen-back episodes can show played songs as chapters in Now Playing.
This is Goolaerts’ first merged contribution to the Music Assistant server. Welcome, Bram—and congratulations on landing an unusually complete first PR.

articles.title: Gas and batteries land in Home Assistant’s iOS energy widget
articles.dek: Merged iOS work expands the glanceable energy view from grid and solar to four parts of a household’s energy picture.
body: Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves expanded the Home Assistant iOS energy widget beyond grid and solar. The merged design stacks battery discharge above the chart axis and charging below it; gas appears as a separate figure because homes may measure it by volume rather than energy.

The merged widget code uses the same consumption math as the energy dashboard, so charging a battery is not also counted as household demand. It combines electricity and gas costs, and all four sources still fit on the small widget and Lock Screen accessories.
The work continues Gonçalves’s August run on the widget, after Lock Screen sizing, a reload action for missing data and clearer period and refresh-time information landed earlier in the month.
articles.continuity: Part of a month-long series improving Home Assistant’s energy widgets across iPhone and Lock Screen layouts.

articles.title: Bluetooth repair clears connections left by removed adapters
articles.dek: A merged library fix drops links that depended on a disabled or removed adapter, allowing devices to reconnect cleanly.
body: Radek Podgorny traced a stubborn Bluetooth state mismatch to scanner removal. Home Assistant cleared its bookkeeping when an adapter disappeared, but connections made through that adapter could remain alive, continuing to deliver notifications while occupying a slot the system believed was free.

The repair disconnects clients that still depend on an adapter when that adapter is removed, while leaving alone any device that has already found another route. It covers local adapters and ESPHome Bluetooth proxies.

Podgorny verified the local path on real BlueZ hardware: disabling the adapter dropped the kernel link, and enabling it again allowed a clean reconnect. The remote-proxy path has automated coverage but was not part of that hardware test.

articles.title: A Music Assistant fix keeps collaboration tracks in YouTube Music albums
articles.dek: Merged server work stops songs from silently disappearing when YouTube Music returns a collaborator without an artist ID.
body: Some YouTube Music collaboration tracks arrive without an artist ID. Music Assistant treated that missing identifier as invalid and quietly left the song out of its album listing; the reported album lost four tracks this way.
Marvin Schenkel’s merged repair follows YouTube Music’s own fallback: when none of a track’s credited artists can be matched, Music Assistant uses the album artist instead of dropping the track.

articles.title: Two beta-period fixes protect work in Home Assistant’s editors
articles.dek: Merged frontend repairs keep one editor’s state out of another and preserve automation configuration when a device is replaced.
body: Home Assistant entered its September beta period last week with two closely related frontend repairs aimed at preserving work in its editors.

One merged fix stops editor state from leaking when people switch between automations, scripts or scenes. Another keeps an automation’s existing configuration when one of its devices is replaced, instead of making that carefully built setup collateral damage.
Together, the changes tighten the boundary between editing one configuration and altering another. They are merged groundwork for a safer editing experience as the September release approaches.
articles.continuity: The recap follows two frontend fixes with one reader outcome: preserving existing Home Assistant editor work during beta.
